criteria.name: Problem 1a
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 1a (1 pt). Statement: One might guess that in most cases, E(n,k )≈ n k . In light of this guess, deﬁne the ineﬃciency of the ordered pair (n,k ), denoted I(n,k ), as I(n,k ) =E(n,k )− n k if E(n,k )̸=∞. If E(n,k ) =∞, then by convention, I(n,k ) is undeﬁned. 8. a. criteria.name: Problem 1d

criteria.name: Problem 1e
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 1e (4 pts). Statement: 9. Let S be the set of values of I(n,k ) for all n,k for which k < n 2 and I(n,k ) is deﬁned. Find the least upper bound of S. Prove that your answer is correct.

criteria.name: Problem 1f
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 1f (4 pts). Statement: 10. Find two distinct non-integral positive rational numbers that are not the ineﬃciency of any ordered pair. That is, ﬁnd positive rational numbers q1 andq2 withq1̸=q2 such that neither q1 norq2 is an integer and such that neither q1 nor q2 is I(n,k ) for any integers n and k. Prove that your answers are correct.
